raw.assessment: The incumbent supplies full-motion, embedded-caption previews and retained history, supporting timing checks and access to delivered versions. It achieved the 15-minute target in 20/30 sessions, below the required 27/30. H1-O7 limits any claim that full rendering inherently prevents success: nine single-correction sessions succeeded in five to 11 minutes without version uncertainty. Multiple saves, reversed completion order and mismatched downloads support investigating identification and input binding; they do not establish their causal contribution or a computing shortage. All observations are stipulated synthetic evidence.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: binding each preview request to immutable video and caption snapshots, and displaying that pair consistently through request, history and download, would reduce unintended combinations and identification errors.
openings.delta: Replace reliance on caption filenames and completion numbers with an explicit source-pair identity and request order; retain the last delivered pair and its original text.
openings.prediction: With deliberately reversed completion order and a changed video cut, editors select the requested pair and downloaded hashes match its recorded inputs.
openings.probe: Prototype in private staging with demonstration footage; test two rapid caption edits and a video replacement with both editors. Check actual render inputs, selected download and continued retrieval of the delivered version.
assumptions: Immutable input references can be implemented within four engineer-days and tested within one editor-day and the processing allowance.
Editors can recognize the displayed pair; hash correctness alone cannot establish their intent.

openings.claim: Do late sessions lose most time before the intended preview becomes available, or after availability while editors identify and inspect it?
openings.delta: Distinguishes render-path delay from interpretation delay before choosing a further intervention.
openings.prediction: Render-path limitation produces long final-edit-to-availability intervals; identification limitation produces short availability intervals followed by long selection intervals and repeated downloads.
openings.probe: Match final edits to intended input pairs in retained events where possible, and time availability, selection and viewing in private staging walkthroughs. Compare repeated-edit scenarios with the supplied single-correction limiting case; mark unidentifiable historical pairs unresolved.
assumptions: A bounded walkthrough and event review fit the existing labor allowance.
Staging findings cannot establish unmeasured festival demand or the required 30-session success rate.

raw.assessment: The observations establish delay and version mismatches, but do not identify their causes. A speculative capability is immediate, identifiable playback of a frozen video-and-caption pair. Its feasibility and agreement with embedded captions remain unproven.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: a private browser preview could play a frozen video cut with overlaid captions immediately after editing, while an approved pair still produces the required embedded-caption delivery. Keep the last delivered video and its original caption snapshot accessible.
openings.delta: Decouple wording-and-timing inspection from full rendering. Dependencies are privately playable footage, immutable pair identifiers, a cue renderer, and agreement between its timing/layout and the embedding worker. The presently testable partial capability is replaying one frozen pair through both paths.
openings.prediction: If render waiting dominates and the two renderers agree, editors will identify and inspect the final pair sooner, without accepting wording or timing that differs in the embedded output.
openings.probe: Use retained demonstration footage on private staging: compare overlay and embedded playback at cue boundaries, then time two editors making single and repeated corrections. Measure disagreement and time separately. Proceed only within four engineer-days, one editor-day and 80 total weekly processing hours; otherwise retain the incumbent.
assumptions: An existing private playback path can be reused within the budget.
Overlay fidelity is sufficient for the editors' actual inspection tasks.

openings.claim: Do unexpected previews arise from capturing the wrong input pair, or from selecting an unexpected completed preview?
openings.delta: Separate input capture from history interpretation using a boundary-by-boundary identity trace.
openings.prediction: A capture problem produces divergence before rendering; a selection problem preserves the intended request through worker output but diverges at download selection.
openings.probe: Within the same staging budget, record editor-confirmed video/caption hashes at request, worker input, completion and download while deliberately reversing completion order. Locate the first divergence; allow both causes or neither.
assumptions: Editors can confirm the intended pair independently of completion numbering.
Staging behavior is informative but cannot establish the 30-session success target.

openings.claim: Bind requests to immutable video/caption snapshots; show pair identity and request order through download.
openings.discriminator: Reversed completions preserve intended selection and input hashes.
openings.fit: uncertain; retain delivered pair and original wording
openings.probe: Private staging: both editors, rapid edits, replacement cut, delivered-version retrieval.
openings.uncertainty: Budget feasibility and editors' recognition; hashes alone cannot prove intent.

openings.claim: Separate render waiting from identification and inspection delay.
openings.probe: Review events and time single/repeated-edit walkthroughs; leave unidentified historical pairs unresolved.
openings.uncertainty: Festival demand and 30-session performance remain unestablished.

openings.claim: Immediately overlay captions on a frozen private video pair; render approved pairs into required embedded-caption format.
openings.discriminator: Faster inspection only if waiting dominates and overlay agrees with embedded playback.
openings.probe: Compare cue boundaries, timing/layout and editor correction times; reuse private playback within four engineer-days, one editor-day, 80 total weekly processing hours or retain incumbent.
openings.uncertainty: Playback reuse and inspection fidelity unproven.

openings.claim: Distinguish wrong input capture from unexpected history selection.
openings.discriminator: First divergence before worker input versus at download; both or neither possible.
openings.probe: Trace editor-confirmed hashes at request, worker, completion and download under reversed completion order.
openings.uncertainty: Independent intent confirmation and staging generalizability.

post_distill.decision: Prioritize bounded private diagnostics and identity prototype; gate overlay on waiting and fidelity evidence. Share stipulated labor/compute limits across probes. Synthetic baseline 20/30 versus required 27/30; nine successful single-correction sessions limit generalization. No computing shortage established.
